title: Explaining why a statistical diagram leads to misinterpretation of data
summary: Detect distorted scales, misleading symbols, missing context and selective reporting.
objectives: Identify common features that distort statistical diagrams.
Quantify how a truncated scale or resized symbol exaggerates change.
Recommend a fair scale, label set and time window.

blocks.text: A fair diagram uses consistent intervals, clear labels and enough context. A truncated axis can magnify small differences. Enlarging both dimensions of a picture changes its area, and enlarging three dimensions changes its volume. Selective dates can hide the broader pattern.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: Values 52 and 56 are drawn above a baseline of 50. Compare their displayed heights.

sections.verification_note: Check the title, scale, key, labels and total before accepting the interpretation.

prompt.text: A square icon's side is doubled. By what factor does its area grow?

feedback.text: Area scales with the square of length, so 2² = 4.

blocks.text: Identify the data structure and purpose, read every scale and key carefully, calculate from the stated values, then check whether the display gives an accurate and complete impression.
